chapter: Chicago, Villa Venice and Louis Armstrong
title: Armstrong's contract with Collins and Rockwell
summary: Budd explains how Armstrong's lawyer Collins held power of attorney and obliged him to pay Rockwell $150 a week after his California reefer arrest.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: So we said no, we want our whole $40.00, man. We've been out on this road, man, working with Louis Armstrong? You've got to be kidding. Well he had this guy Collins and his wife, and Collins was an old law firm in Chicago, called Collins and Collins, and how Louis got situated with Collins and Collins was that when he got into this trouble out in California, on this reefer rap, it was sent to jail, he was working for Rockwell, Rockwell and O'Keefe, you know. He was working for Rockwell.
How much time did Louis do? About a month or so?
He did a little more time than that.

Yeah, he did -- he did maybe three, I don't know. I'm not too positive about that. But anyway, Rockwell sent Collins out there to get him out of jail. In doing so Collins had tricked Louis, and Louis had signed up with Collins, and -- but in this thing Collins had stipulated that Louis had to pay Rockwell $150.00 a week as long as he worked for --
And so Collins had complete power of attorney, and Louis didn't really understand what that was all about, because after we had made this tour -- and I'll get back to Cincinnati and --
Oh, go ahead, you go ahead and --
